questions.question_english: A recognized unaided private school forces its students to pay an "annual development charge" which constitutes 50% of the tuition fee. What is the legal provision regarding this under the DSEA & R 1973 and Supreme Court judgments?
options_english: Fully permissible provided the school provides fully air-conditioned facilities.
Cannot exceed 15% of tuition fee and kept separately for capital costs.
Development charges are entirely illegal and cannot be levied under any norm.
The school can levy any fee amount provided an official receipt is issued.
questions.explanation_english: The keyed answer is B: the development charge is subject to the stated ceiling and must be accounted for separately for permitted capital purposes. Calling a levy a 'development charge' does not remove it from fee regulation, and issuing a receipt alone does not make an otherwise excessive charge lawful. The school must comply with the applicable fee orders, accounting requirements and judicial directions; amenities such as air-conditioning do not independently validate an unrestricted levy.

questions.question_english: An aided private school decides to dismiss a confirmed PGT due to alleged financial irregularities. The managing committee completes the departmental inquiry and immediately issues a dismissal letter without informing the Directorate of Education. How should this action be evaluated based on DSEA 1973?
options_english: The action is void because dismissal requires prior approval of the Director.
The action is legally sound because the managing committee is the sole disciplinary authority.
The action is valid provided the Parent- Teacher Association formally approves the dismissal.
The action is valid only if the accused teacher explicitly confesses to the financial irregularities.
questions.explanation_english: The action is void because dismissal requires prior approval of the Director. Under Section 8(2) of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973, no confirmed employee of a recognized aided private school can be dismissed, removed, or reduced in rank without prior written approval from the Director of Education. Dismissal orders issued unilaterally by managing committees without obtaining statutory DoE approval are legally void, unenforceable, and invalid from inception.
questions.explanation_hindi: धारा 8(2) के अंतर्गत मान्यता-प्राप्त सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालय के स्थायी कर्मचारी की बर्खास्तगी के लिए आवश्यक वैधानिक स्वीकृति की अनदेखी नहीं की जा सकती। विभागीय जाँच पूरी कर लेना अपने-आप में आवश्यक स्वीकृति का विकल्प नहीं है। इसलिए निदेशक की पूर्व स्वीकृति के बिना जारी किया गया बर्खास्तगी-पत्र वैधानिक प्रक्रिया की कमी से प्रभावित होगा।
